description: After fz-kdt.177.12 makes recursive runtime predicates finite and evaluable on all doors, make runtime transport finite without truncating sibling structure. Boundary demand cuts only an active Ty to RuntimeDemand::whole; layout construction cuts only an active (Ty, RuntimeDemand) relation to a boxed ValueRef lane. The boundary retains each finite outer prefix and applies no depth budget. Reuse the canonical regular test constructors and prove mixed recursive tuple/list/callable shapes terminate with deterministic finite layouts. The direct predicate and three-door evaluator contract belongs to fz-kdt.177.12; this ticket consumes it and completes transport before recursive typedefs enter production.

comments.text: 2026-09-17 spike/audit: ground projection is unsound. Runtime predicates retain observable nested tuple/list/capture questions across interpreter, JIT, AOT; today their by-value tree and shared native inliner diverge on a μ type before transport. WIP cf12208d1 proves the transport half: cut only active Ty -> whole demand and active (Ty, RuntimeDemand) -> boxed ValueRef, preserving siblings. Audit rejected shipping it separately because mixed recursive unions/lists/captures reach runtime_type_predicate first. Complete .177.7 atomically with a finite predicate component/graph, pair-keyed predicate relations, and shared cyclic CFG lowering for prim + receive; fold the transport cuts into that commit. No budget or interpreter-only path is sound.

2026-09-17 decomposition correction: the preceding comment describes the combined pre-spike understanding. fz-kdt.177.12 now owns the finite predicate graph and shared all-door evaluator; this ticket remains the transport-only successor and is blocked by .12. WIP cf12208d1 stays unpushed as the transport prototype.

title: Recursive transport boundary cuts cycles to boxed values
